what: Live end-to-end probe of Lifeline's cross-chain rescue: a callback recipient on Base Sepolia runs into debt at the real callback proxy, Lifeline (Lasna) sees the proxy's BlacklistContract event, a LifelineFunder on Base pays the debt, and the recipient's callbacks resume. Run 2026-11-23.

timeline.event: trigger reacts to Cron10 and requests a callback to the sink
callback #1 delivered: sink pings (state changes), is then charged with no reserves, goes into debt and the proxy emits BlacklistContract(sink)
Lifeline reacts to the proxy's BlacklistContract and requests a rescue callback
LifelineFunder.rescue pays the debt plus top-up; proxy emits WhitelistContract(sink)
next callback delivered and executed: the recipient is live again

noteOnTiming: Base block timestamps resolve to 1 s (about 5 blocks per second), so these are approximate to one second.
findings: The Base callback proxy emits BlacklistContract(address indexed) / WhitelistContract(address indexed) for callback recipients, and Lasna reactive contracts can subscribe to them per target (topic1 = target).
A recipient is charged AFTER its callback runs. The first callback therefore executes; the recipient is blacklisted afterwards.

A recipient receives gasLimit - (extraGas 80,000 + maxChargeGas 50,000) of gas. A 200,000 request left about 70,000: a cold first-write ping ran out of gas, emitted CallbackFailure, and was still billed. Five such callbacks drained the sink's reserve with no state change. Rerun with 500,000 worked.
LifelineFunder.rescue ran inside the 300,000 gas request and cleared the debt in one callback.

firstAttemptThatFailedForGas.result: rescue loop worked (blacklist tx 0xa84c913b46a328c5608987afff67f2fa45a22db54c350f71392af19be3d15d04, rescued in 0x9985a6c904772d354f21d358507ab51efa7b3bbbb804de469b5d96debfffdf04) but the sink's own ping callbacks ran out of gas because the probe requested only 200,000
